operations: JSE-listed (pending delisting - see status); plants at Wadeville, Clayville, Aeroton/Bangalore and Bloemfontein; head office Bryanston/Midrand
scale_note: Renewable energy capacity installed 2,675 kW; solar PV generated 3,332 MWh FY24 (+30% YoY), 6% of Group energy from solar (up from 5%); solar PV commissioned at Bloemfontein site; independent engineering company appointed to pursue wheeling agreements of green energy (FY24 Integrated Report, no name given); diesel consumption fell with reduced loadshedding FY24. Jul 2025: India's Natco Pharma agreed to acquire all shares not held by Bidvest via scheme of arrangement, delisting from JSE with Bidvest as controlling shareholder - transaction still completing as at Sep 2026.

operations: JSE-listed group HQ at Aspen Place, La Lucia Ridge, Durban; 24 manufacturing facilities at 15 sites incl. Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth) steriles plant
scale_note: Gqeberha plant sources ~8% of electricity from on-site solar PV, targeted full grid independence within 18 months per Feb 2023 press interview (stale, not confirmed achieved) https://www.businessday.co.za/bd/national/health/2023-02-14-aspen-pharmacare-aims-to-be-off-power-grid-in-18-months/ ; Group-wide renewable energy share of total energy consumption 10.58% in FY2025 (up 66% since FY2023 but down 1.09% YoY); renewable electricity reported at 18% in FY2024; overall carbon emissions down 28.4% over five years per Aspen sustainability reporting https://www.aspenpharma.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Aspen-2023-Sustainability-and-ESG-Data-Supplement.pdf ; no wheeling agreement or PPA publicly disclosed as at Sep 2026.

operations: State-linked (public-private partnership) human vaccine manufacturer; single manufacturing plant in the Cape Town area (Pinelands/Green Point); Exec team incl. Dr Morena Makhoana (CEO), Craig Mitchell (CFO), Mark MacNaughton (COO) per https://biovac.co.za/executive-team/
scale_note: Major expansion under way as at 2026: $253m programme (incl EUR75m/R1.45bn EIB Group quasi-equity, $20m IFC loan, $20m/R327m AFD and Proparco funding, $15m AfDB) to build end-to-end vaccine manufacturing incl. oral cholera vaccine plant due 2028, lifting total capacity to 500m doses/year https://www.businessday.co.za/news/health/2026-04-16-biovac-launches-ambitious-new-expansion-plan/ ; company states facility designed with energy-efficient systems but no MW solar, wheeling/PPA deal or net-zero target publicly disclosed as at Sep 2026.

operations: Owns and manages 7 private hospitals (incl. Botshelong-Empilweni, Vosloorus, and a day clinic opened in Johannesburg CBD) serving mainly township/peri-urban communities; ~2600 employees; founded 1992 by Dr K O P Matseke. Company website unreachable for verification (connection refused) as at Sep 2026; no named CEO/executive team found on any public source reached.
scale_note: No public disclosure found of solar installations, wheeling/PPA deals, MW capacity, net-zero target or diesel generator spend for Clinix specifically; sector-wide context: SA government costed R10.1bn capex to solarise 137 public hospitals, diesel ~4x cost of Eskom power per load-shedding coverage https://businesstech.co.za/news/government/646985/government-considering-solar-for-hospitals-in-south-africa/ (context only, not Clinix-specific).

operations: Bundle of three separately-branded private pathology groups: Lancet Laboratories (HQ Johannesburg, lancet.co.za), Ampath Laboratories (HQ Centurion, Pretoria, ampath.co.za), PathCare (HQ Cape Town, founded 1922, pathcare.co.za); each operates a national branch-laboratory network across SA rather than a single plant.
scale_note: Paris-based Cerba Healthcare (owned by PSP Investments and Partners Group) agreed a ~$123m deal in Jan 2019 for African lab assets and holds a 51% stake in the Cerba-Lancet Africa joint venture covering 11 African countries, though this excludes Lancet's core South African operations https://www.engineeringnews.co.za/article/cerba-lancet-are-said-to-agree-africa-deal-for-123m-2019-01-11 ; no MW solar, wheeling/PPA, net-zero target or diesel-generator spend publicly disclosed for any of the three labs as at Sep 2026; no named executives with titles found on any of the three companies' own leadership pages (none publish a leadership/management page with names) - CEO/MD names circulating for Ampath and PathCare on third-party recruiter/data-broker sites were not used as they are not company-published sources.

operations: JSE-listed group (Life Healthcare Group Holdings Ltd); Southern Africa division is the core SA hospital network after disposal of UK's Alliance Medical Group in FY24; Group CEO Peter Wharton-Hood, Group CFO Pieter van der Westhuizen (also covers IT/cyber), COO Craig Koekemoer, per Business Day 11 Apr 2024 https://www.businessday.co.za/bd/companies/healthcare/2024-04-11-life-healthcare-shakes-up-its-executive/ ; no email found on official pages for these three, so not written as contacts.
scale_note: Completed procurement process for a 9.3 MWp solar installation across the hospital portfolio (FY2025); Scope 1 emissions down 37.4% and Scope 3 down 75.8% driven by reduced diesel usage and waste diversion; national general-waste recycling programme rolled out to 39 hospitals in FY2025 (43%/2,074 tonnes of waste recycled); target of zero general waste to landfill by 2030 per Life Healthcare Sustainability Report 2025 https://www.lifehealthcare.co.za/media/4221/life_healthcare_sustainability_report_2025_158_20251208_final_interactive.pdf ; no wheeling/PPA deal named as signed as at Sep 2026.

operations: Southern Africa division of Mediclinic Group (Remgro-linked, taken private 2023 in Remgro/MSC Mediterranean Shipping consortium buyout); operates acute-care private hospitals in South Africa and Namibia; Exec team per official site https://mediclinic.co.za/en/corporate/about-mediclinic-southern-africa/executive-management.html : Braam Joubert (Chief Executive Officer), Nazeer Wadee (Chief Financial Officer), Dr Gerrit de Villiers (Chief Operating Officer); Kobus Jonck named General Manager of Infrastructure in a 2021 solar-project article (role may be stale) https://renewafrica.biz/news/solar/mediclinic-contracts-moshesh-to-power-six-hospitals-with-solar/ ; no emails published for any of these, so none written as contacts.
scale_note: 12-year PPA (option to extend to 25 years) signed with Moshesh Partners (black-owned renewable asset manager, RECI Fund 1) and installer ACES Africa for rooftop solar across six Mediclinic hospitals incl. Vergelegen and Durbanville, ~4,100,000 kWh/year combined, synced with generators and Eskom supply to prioritise solar during outages, installed Jun-Dec 2021 https://renewafrica.biz/news/solar/mediclinic-contracts-moshesh-to-power-six-hospitals-with-solar/ ; newest hospital (George, Garden Route, opened/profiled Apr 2026) built with 600kW peak rooftop solar covering ~60% of roof space, heat-recovery and water-recycling systems, ~75% waste diversion from landfill https://www.mediclinic.co.za/en/foh-corporate/news/designing-with-the-environment-in-mind.html

operations: National Hospital Network (NHN) is an association/network (est. 1996) of independently-owned private hospitals in South Africa - not a single operating company - covering acute, day, ophthalmology, psychiatry and sub-acute/rehab facilities; named staff per official site https://nhn.co.za/management-2-2/ : Neil Nair (CEO), Loedt Zemanay (Group Operations Manager); no individual emails published (only info@nhn.co.za switchboard). Joint Medical Holdings (JMH) could not be independently verified or connected to NHN from any official source reached - JMH's own site (jointmedicalholdings.co.za) refused connection from this tool and no NHN page names JMH; this pairing needs confirmation before outreach.
scale_note: No hospital count, bed count, solar MW, wheeling/PPA, net-zero target or diesel spend publicly disclosed by NHN as a network (each member hospital is independently owned and likely manages its own energy procurement); no equivalent data found for Joint Medical Holdings.

operations: JSE-listed Netcare Limited; Board and Exco per Netcare Integrated Report 2025 (Board of Directors excerpt) https://www.netcare.co.za/Portals/0/OneNetcare/Documents/Netcare-Board-of-directors.pdf : Dr Richard Friedland (Chief executive officer, chairs Executive, Environmental Sustainability and AI committees), Melanie Da Costa (Director of strategy, health policy and CEO designate), Keith Gibson (Chief financial officer, chairs Finance and Investment, Working Capital and Procurement committees), Dr Erich Bock (Managing director - Hospital Division); no individual emails found on any official page reached, so none written as contacts - flag Friedland, Da Costa, Gibson and Bock for Apollo enrichment.
scale_note: Solar PV installed at 72 Group sites, described by Netcare as the second-largest commercial solar PV undertaking in South Africa https://www.netcare.co.za/who-we-are/sustainability ; 35% reduction in energy intensity per bed achieved in sustainability Phase 1; Phase 2 target is Scope 2 emissions to zero via 100% renewable electricity and a combined 84% reduction in Scope 1+2 emissions, both by 2030; separately, Oct 2023 agreement with NOA Group Trading to wheel wind and solar electricity (via grid wheeling) to 6 Netcare facilities from Q1 2026, covering up to 100% of those sites' consumption (~11% or 22 GWh/year of Group total), lifting Group renewable share to ~26% https://cleantechnica.com/2023/10/03/south-africas-netcare-will-procure-electricity-for-6-of-its-facilities-from-wind-solar-farms/ (facility names not disclosed in this article).

operations: State entity (Schedule 3A public entity under the Department of Health) operating a national network of public pathology laboratories serving all state hospitals and clinics - cited as 265 laboratories (Wikipedia, undated) vs 226 labs / ~1,500 test types per a 2019 Africa Outlook interview with then-acting CEO Dr Karmani Chetty https://www.africaoutlookmag.com/company-profiles/1082-national-health-laboratory-service-nhls (stale, confidence low); ~8,000 employees. Current CEO as at 2025 is Prof Koleka Mlisana (appointed 2024), confirmed on NHLS's own Board of Directors page (dated 15 Aug 2025, accessed via cached search snippet - direct fetch of nhls.ac.za blocked by an invalid/unverifiable TLS certificate from this tool) and independently quoted as CEO in Daily Maverick 21 Mar 2025 and Health-e News 1 Jul 2024; no email found for her on any source reached, so not written as a contact. A CFO referred to only as 'Kammy' (surname not found) manages finance incl. facilities and supply chain per nhls.ac.za/about-us/executive-management-3/ (cached snippet dated 17 Aug 2023) - full name not confirmed, so not written as a contact.
scale_note: NHLS's own Strategic Plan 2025-2030 states the organisation is a 'net energy consumer and a waste producer' and that achieving sustainability 'will necessitate innovative approaches to laboratory design' (source: nhls.ac.za, cached snippet, Apr 2025) - no MW of solar, wheeling agreement, PPA, net-zero target or diesel-generator spend publicly disclosed as at Sep 2026; prior budget figures show NHLS budget declining from R1.082bn (2019/20) to R641.8m (2021/22) per Wikipedia.
